design_rationale: Explicit cluster randomization of nine Cree communities to test or control conditions via a constrained envelope-draw procedure conducted over community radio ("Nine Cree communities in Quebec, Canada were randomly allocated to test or control"; trial registration ISRCTN41467632).

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was genuinely random (public constrained envelope draw, concealed until drawn, performed before participant recruitment), but with only 9 clusters several prognostically relevant baseline characteristics differed notably between arms, raising concerns about chance imbalance (addressed only by post hoc covariate adjustment).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "However, despite the random assignment of communities, fewer test mothers had already delivered at time of enrollment (19.2% vs. 40.0%), had visited a dentist for toothache (35.5% vs. 50.0%), and had other children with a previous tooth extraction (34.1% vs. 48.9%)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Mothers and interveners were unblinded and the trial reports substantial implementation/fidelity problems (staff turnover, variable session attendance, privilege cards not honored), although analyses appear to follow the as-randomized groups consistent with a pragmatic effectiveness design.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Mothers and interveners were aware of their community's allocation... Certainly, challenges related to treatment fidelity are acknowledged (Borrelli, 2011)... not all clinics honored the cards."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 241/272 (89%) with similar attrition in both arms (16% test, 7% control is modest in absolute numbers), making bias from missingness unlikely to materially alter the result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "From January 2005 to October 2007, 272 mothers (131 test, 141 control) were recruited. At follow-up, 241 children were examined for caries (110 test, 131 control)."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary caries outcome was assessed clinically with standard (Pitts) criteria by calibrated examiners blinded to allocation, applied identically in both arms; parent-reported quality-of-life secondary outcomes are more susceptible but are not the primary outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "clinical data were collected by calibrated examiners, masked to the community's assignment... The examiners were blinded to allocation and were unfamiliar with the intervention."

domain_judgments.rationale: The pre-specified primary outcome (d2-level caries) is clearly reported as null and the trial was registered with a published protocol, but the emphasis in the abstract/conclusions rests on multiple exploratory outcome definitions, adjusted/unadjusted models, and a post hoc dose (number-of-sessions, median-split) subgroup analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Exploratory analyses (Table 1) suggested a substantial benefit of the intervention in controlling for a higher severity of disease... Additional exploratory analyses suggested that the treatment effect might be very large for participants who attended 4 or more MI-style sessions vs. 3 or fewer"

overall_summary: This registered cluster-randomized pragmatic trial used a transparent randomization procedure, blinded calibrated examiners, and had low attrition, but concerns remain from baseline imbalances across only nine clusters, unblinded mothers/interveners with acknowledged fidelity problems, and heavy reliance on exploratory/post hoc analyses (severity thresholds, dose subgroups) to support the positive conclusions. No single domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is 'some concerns'.

design_rationale: Explicit random allocation is described: 579 mother-newborn dyads were randomized 1:1 to MI+ECS vs ECS using a stratified blocked randomization design with a random number generator, and the trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01116726).

domain_judgments.rationale: A computer-based random number generator with stratification and random permuted blocks generated the sequence, allocation was concealed by obtaining assignment via telephone from a remote central staff member only after consent/enrollment, and baseline characteristics were well balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A stratified blocked randomization design employed a random number generator, with stratification based on the age of the mother. Randomly selected block sizes of 2 or 4 were used. Randomization was implemented by telephone between field staff enrolling the participants and a staff member at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus. Field staff obtained informed consent and enrolled participants prior to obtaining group assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and interventionists were necessarily unblinded, which is especially relevant for the self-reported knowledge/behavior secondary outcomes, though adherence was high (88% completed ≥3 of 4 sessions), fidelity was formally monitored, and a modified intention-to-treat analysis was used; the "modified" ITT dropped a small unspecified number of dyads after randomization.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to the nature of the intervention, providers and participants could not be masked in this trial. ... We call the analysis "modified intention to treat" because a small percentage of the mother-child dyads were dropped after randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Approximately 16-20% of dyads lacked 36-month primary outcome data (232/290 and 238/289 examined at 36 mo), and although retention was balanced across arms and mixed-effects models were used, no sensitivity analysis or comparison of completers versus dropouts is reported to demonstrate that missingness did not bias the caries results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 579 dyads (290 MI + ECS, 289 ECS) completed the baseline activities, and 84% completed the 36-mo assessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (dmfs) was assessed by calibrated dental examiners blinded to group assignment with documented inter-examiner reliability (kappa ≥0.75) and identical procedures in both arms; the subjective self-reported knowledge/behavior secondary outcomes are more vulnerable, but the primary outcome measurement is at low risk.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was the dmfs measure of decayed, missing, or filled primary tooth surfaces, measured at months 12, 24, and 36, by calibrated dental examiners masked to group assignment ... minimum tooth surface-level agreement between each calibrated examiner and the gold standard examiner was a Cohen's kappa ≥0.75

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT01116726) with a previously published design/protocol and pre-specified primary outcome (dmfs) and sample-size calculation, and all pre-specified primary and secondary outcomes appear reported, including null findings; minor post hoc analytic simplifications (dropping covariates) were transparently described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Details of the trial design and protocol (Batliner et al. 2014) as well as caries assessment procedures (Warren et al. 2016) were previously published. ... The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01116726).

overall_summary: This well-conducted, pre-registered RCT had robust central randomization, blinded calibrated caries examiners, high intervention adherence and fidelity monitoring, and complete reporting of pre-specified outcomes. Overall risk is "some concerns" because of unavoidable non-blinding of participants/interventionists combined with an incompletely specified "modified" ITT exclusion (D2) and ~16% attrition at 36 months without sensitivity analyses of missingness (D3), though these are unlikely to explain the null primary result.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly reports a parallel-group randomized controlled trial with 1:1 allocation of mother-child pairs: "Random sequence generation was performed by manual (simple) randomization via drawing lots" using Zelen's double-consent design.

domain_judgments.rationale: Random sequence generation by drawing lots is plausibly random and baseline characteristics appeared similar, but allocation concealment is not described and the Zelen design with post-randomization consent/exclusions (and unequal group sizes 40 vs 35) raises concerns about the integrity of allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Random sequence generation was performed by manual (simple) randomization via drawing lots." ... "Zelen's randomization with double consent was used ... randomization occurs before consent."

domain_judgments.rationale: Open-label behavioural intervention where mothers and providers knew allocation (usual-care mothers were unaware of the trial altogether), several randomized participants did not receive their allocated intervention, and the analysis was per-protocol excluding 20 randomized pairs rather than intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "blinding of participants that received the intervention was not possible due to Zelen's randomization" ... "our analyses were based on a per-protocol analysis, and not on an intention-to-treat analysis."

domain_judgments.rationale: Roughly 27% of randomized pairs were excluded/lost to follow-up (30% intervention, 23% usual care), no sensitivity or imputation analysis was performed, and missingness in a behaviourally driven outcome could plausibly depend on the true outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Of the 75 mother-child pairs included at baseline, 55 (73%) had a complete assessment after 12 months: 28 out of 40 (70%) in the intervention group and 27 out of 35 (77%) in the usual care group." ... "the dropout rate was very high in both groups"

domain_judgments.rationale: The composite primary outcome relies largely on maternal self-report of hygiene/diet plus unblinded, uncalibrated clinical examination by a single assessor aware of allocation, making outcome ascertainment susceptible to both social-desirability and detection bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "the outcome assessor was not blinded to group allocation, which could introduce some degree of detection bias" ... "Assessments were conducted based on professional experience ... with no prior calibration being performed."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was only retrospectively registered and the primary outcome relies on an author-modified, non-validated caries-risk score alongside multiple secondary outcomes, so selective definition/reporting of results cannot be excluded, although all pre-specified-type outcomes appear reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "retrospectively registered at the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials [ReBEC]: RBR-74qm3m" ... "we created a simplified score based on two domains"

overall_summary: Overall high risk of bias, driven by the unblinded behavioural design analysed per-protocol (D2), high and differential attrition (~27% of randomized pairs excluded, D3), and outcome assessment by a single unblinded, uncalibrated examiner using largely self-reported components (D4). Concerns about allocation concealment under Zelen randomization and retrospective registration with an author-modified composite outcome compound the judgment.

design_rationale: The authors explicitly describe a randomized controlled trial using Zelen's double-consent design with a random number table to allocate nulliparous women to test or control groups, plus a second randomization of the test group into subgroups A and B.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random number table generated the allocation sequence, but under the Zelen double-consent design allocation preceded and was disclosed at consent (no concealment, and the same researcher recruited and allocated), and two baseline characteristics differed significantly between arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Zelen's design with double consent and a random number table (11–13) was used to allocate women into test or control groups before their participation was sought." ... "The only significant differences between the groups at baseline were in the use of dental floss (31.6% in the test group used versus 22.6% women in the control group; chisquare P < 0.01) and in the use of alcoholic drinks during the pregnancy (12.4% in the test group compared with 7.4% in the control group; chisquare P < 0.05)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Mothers and the researcher were necessarily aware of allocation (inherent to a behavioural/educational intervention), a few participants crossed from control to test, and the analysis appears to be of participants as treated/followed rather than a clearly described intention-to-treat analysis; however, deviations were few (0.8%) and the intervention itself was delivered as planned.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Lack of blinding (14) and potential loss of statistical power (if many participants refuse the allocated group) are the main disadvantages of the design." ... "Only five women (0.8%) from all women recruited to the trial changed the group to which they were randomly allocated once they received information about the aims of the trial. All moved from the control group to the test group."

domain_judgments.rationale: Nearly 30% of outcome data were missing, attrition was differential between arms (74.4% vs 66.8% retention), and in the control group loss was selectively greater among younger and less-educated mothers — precisely the group at highest caries risk — so missingness could plausibly inflate the apparent effect; no sensitivity or imputation analysis was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The overall retention thorough to the examination was 70.6%, higher in the test group (74.4%) than in the control group (66.8%; Table 1)." ... "However, in the control group losses to follow-up were higher among younger and less educated mothers (chi-square P < 0.01)."

domain_judgments.rationale: The single examiner was the same author who recruited mothers and delivered the intervention, so blinding was only nominally supported by receptionist scheduling, the subjective outcome (visually diagnosed noncavitated lesions) is highly susceptible to assessor knowledge, and no reliability data were collected.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Thirdly, all mothers were recruited and the intervention administered by the same author as who conducted the dental examinations. Any recall of group assignment of individual mothers could have biased the dental observations." ... "Secondly, no test–retest reliability information was collected."

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or protocol is cited, multiple case definitions (noncavitated+cavitated versus cavitated only) and multiple regression models were available, and the headline conclusion rests on the definition that reached significance, though the alternative definition was transparently reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "If a case definition based on cavitation only was applied, the number of cases shrank to approximately one-quarter. While the incidence was greater in the control group (1.9%) than in the test group (0.4%), it was not significant."

overall_summary: Although allocation used a random number table, the trial is at high risk of bias overall because ~30% of participants were missing at outcome assessment with differential and socially patterned attrition (greater loss among younger, less-educated control mothers), and because the single, effectively unblinded examiner was the same author who recruited mothers and delivered the intervention, assessing a subjective visual caries outcome with no reliability data. Unconcealed Zelen allocation, baseline imbalances, and absence of a registered protocol add further concerns.

design_rationale: Explicit parallel-group RCT: "The participants were randomly assigned to 1 of 2 parallel groups (1:1 allocation ratio) after baseline data collection. The random number sequence was generated in Excel by an independent statistician before recruitment," with block size 4 and ClinicalTrials.gov registration (NCT02937194).

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated random sequence by an independent statistician, block randomization with opaque sealed envelopes for concealment, and baseline sociodemographic characteristics did not differ between groups (all P > 0.05).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The random number sequence was generated in Excel by an independent statistician before recruitment. Randomization with a block size of 4 was adopted, and opaque sealed envelopes were used to conceal the allocation."

domain_judgments.rationale: Nearly 25% of families were lost by the 3-year follow-up (436/580) with further losses in regression models (n ≈ 383–392); attrition was anticipated in the sample-size calculation and balanced across arms, but no sensitivity/imputation analysis or comparison of completers vs. dropouts is reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "436 toddlers were followed up when they reached 3 y old (test, n = 228; control, n = 208; follow-up rate, 75.2%)"

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and OHE providers were necessarily unblinded (inherent to a counseling intervention) and the authors themselves note possible Hawthorne-type behavior change in controls; no intention-to-treat framing or report of co-interventions/protocol adherence is given, and analyses appear restricted to those followed up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Due to the nature of the intervention, oral health education (OHE) providers and participants could not be masked during this trial." ... "the improved oral hygiene habits of the toddlers in the control group may be attributed to the Hawthorne effect"

domain_judgments.rationale: Clinical caries/plaque outcomes were measured by calibrated examiners blinded to allocation with excellent reliability (low risk), but the behavioral outcomes (feeding habits, toothbrushing) were self-reported by unblinded parents, creating potential social-desirability/reporting bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "dental examiners who collected the clinical data were blinded to the participants’ group allocation" ... "Information related to the feeding habits, oral hygiene practices... was collected by parent-completed questionnaires"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered (NCT02937194) and the primary outcome (ECC prevalence) matches the sample-size calculation, but numerous secondary outcomes and dichotomization thresholds (≥25% VP, ≥5% MS) plus data-driven backward stepwise model building (covariates at P<0.40) allow analytic flexibility not evidently pre-specified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Independent factors as covariates with a P value <0.40 in the bivariate analyses were selected for the model... Backward stepwise selection was employed to remove insignificant variables from the model."

overall_summary: Randomization and allocation concealment were well executed and clinical outcome assessors were blinded with high reliability, but unavoidable non-blinding of participants/providers (with acknowledged Hawthorne effect), ~25% attrition without sensitivity analyses, reliance on parent self-report for behavioral outcomes, and data-driven stepwise modeling of multiple outcomes raise some concerns. No domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is "some concerns".
